newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares fall in featureless market.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares fall in featureless market.

text.p: Egyptian shares returned to their downward trend on Monday in a featureless market with the absence of foreign players, a broker said.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index slipped 4.55 points to close the day at 380.61 on below-average turnover of 43.80 million pounds ($12.90 million).
"The market was overall quiet and foreign clients are absent," Neveen El Tahry of Delta EAB brokerage told Reuters.
"It's a time for buying. Prices are very attractive,"she added.
She said she expected the market to start picking up soon after "all new (mutual) funds begin operation".

A mutual fund, valued at 300 million pounds, is currently open for subscription, a second will be open next month at a minimum value of 50 million pounds and three others worth about 250 million have closed subscription.

Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was still suffering from an announcement that shareholders will have to wait to qualify for their one-for-one free share. The original cut-off date was March 31 but the company postponed it indefinitely because of a technical hitch.
"That was the main reason,"Tahry said of the share's fall.

The company said it would announce a new date as soon as the stock exchange agreed to register the capital increase. Without this the new shares would have had to trade over-the-counter in parallel with the old ones.
The share, the most active in the day, lost 20.00 to close at 465.00, when 3.97 million worth of shares were traded.

But its blue-chip realty sister Heliopolis Housing and Development, which has announced a 25 percent increase in profits for the July-December period, benefited from the report. The share rose 14.00 to 432.00.
Most millers, once the market favourite, went down. Central Egypt Flour Mills was the only exception. The share added 1.35 pounds to end at 61.00.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 600.41 from 615.08 on Sunday. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms also fell to 260.11 from 261.21.
Out of the 95 shares traded on Monday, 31 gained, 32 lost and 32 ended unchanged.
